about: Everything a person can do on the Pursuits screens (src/workspace/spaces-screen.tsx), as DATA the screen runs without knowing which action it is. A new action is one row here. Per action: `id`; `label` and `icon` (a named icon); `tone` (`destructive` tints it); `primary` draws it as the main button where it shows; `shows` lists where it is offered: `list-header` (the Pursuits list, with `list.archived` true while it shows the archived pursuits), `invitation` (each invitation), `space-card` (each pursuit in the list, in its ⋯ menu, with the pursuit's `link`), `header` (a pursuit's header buttons), `menu` (a pursuit's ⋯ menu), `attach` (the composer's attach menu), `composer` (what the message box sends), `item` (each thing in a pursuit), `reaction` (giving or taking back a reaction on a thing, with `asked` holding its `symbol` or own `glyph` and `on`), `member` (each person), `agent` (each agent), `join-link` (the pursuit an invite link opens), `open-to-you` (each pursuit the person is not in that anyone may join), `invite` (each invite link the person made), `rules` (the rules about who may do what in a pursuit). `when` lists conditions that must all hold for it to be offered: a value `read` from the context `is` the given value, or `is_not` it (null means absent). `box` is what it asks for first: `composer` (the message box takes it, with a `chip` above the box and a `placeholder`), `panel` (a small panel with `body` words and `fields`), or `pick` (the picker over `source`: `shareable` for the person's pursuits, decisions and files, `files` for their files). `choices` makes it a choice among a list of the pursuit settings (src/space-settings.json, at the path `from`): each row `{ id, label }` becomes one choice, drawn with a swatch of its id as a colour when `swatches` is true, the one equal to `current` is marked, and the chosen row is read as `chosen`. `confirm` is asked once before it runs. `road` is what it does: `post` sends `body` to /work/api/spaces (or to the page's own road named by `at`, such as /community) followed by `path` (with `pages` it repeats while the answer names a next `cursor`, sending it as `field`), `copy` puts `words` on the clipboard, `screen` changes what this screen shows (`verb`), `sharing` opens the one sharing sheet for the `picked` thing with this pursuit switched on. `queue` asks the person's own AIs for the job row `job` of src/queued-work.json names, with `context` read in; its label and done words come from that row. `reveal` shows one value from the answer once, with a copy button; `copy` puts its words on the clipboard once the road answers. `done` is said when it worked; `after` is what the screen does next (`open-space`, `left`). Words are lists of text and values: `{ "read": { "from": <context>, "key": [<path>] } }`, where the contexts are `pursuit` (with its `description`, `picture` and `colour`), `item`, `thing` (an item's title and who put it there, as shown), `member`, `agent`, `invitation`, `join` (the invite link's `code`), `invite`, `picked`, `asked` (what the box took), `chosen` (the row of `choices` picked), `answer` and `fresh` (a new unique `key`). `people` is the People place's own button. A condition may read what the person may do, as the store answers it from the pursuit's own rules: `space.may.<action>` for the pursuit itself and `item.may.<action>` for one thing (src/space-member-types.mjs), so nothing is offered that the store would refuse.

body: A role can take permissions from other roles. Its permissions decide who can run community events, remove posts, give roles or send digests.
Changing a role keeps its assignments and rules connected to it.
This removes the role only when no one has it, no open invite assigns it, no rule names it and no other role inherits it.
Changing a type keeps the rules and people assigned to it working.
